body:
Fresh independent controls from #2274 at Buster `d4ca72fb4e97ae0a410b0d03258b00495fa45e13`, trusted Clang Release, hosted [run37005042712](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/37005042712), GCC15.2.0-16ubuntu1. Both syntax-only and object operations reproduce:

1. `int main(void){int unused=7;return 0;}` with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`: Buster exits0/no diagnostic; GCC exits1/unused-variable error.
2. Valid main with `-Wbuster-option-does-not-exist`: Buster exits0/no diagnostic; GCC exits1/unrecognized option.
3. `#warning deliberate-warning\nint x;` without Werror: both emit a warning and exit0. Buster does have a warning producer; the failure is policy/capability handling, not absence of every warning.

Source corroboration: `driver.c` accepts arbitrary `-W...` without warning-state semantics. Reuse the existing structured diagnostic records and #1574 parser/preprocessor severity path. Define an explicit supported warning subset and reject unimplemented positive warning requests instead of silently promising them; verify severity in syntax-only and output-producing operations and that errors leave no artifact. Raw exact commands/messages in `probes.json`, verified ZIP SHA256 `619d7c825ece0752362c9f62b56195da2e3641c29e007026c1226ee5ef4642e4`. Untimed probes are valid; no wall-time claim. License/provenance: Buster first-party project license remains unselected at the inspected revision (LICENSES/README.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; #621). GCC compiler GPL-3.0-or-later; this uses GCC as an oracle and copies no compiler source.
